verdict.rationale: Supabase's own CLI covers the headless core of this story. `supabase init` and `supabase start` stand up the full local stack, including Auth, on a machine or in CI. `supabase start` builds the database from migration .sql files, so schema and RLS policies (written as SQL `create policy` statements) can be scripted. The MCP server adds agent-callable `apply_migration` and `create_project` tools. However, the evidence never documents configuring auth providers or settings from the CLI, or pushing migrations to a hosted project in a script. Missing for 10: documented CLI or config-file auth configuration, documented CLI migration push or hosted project provisioning commands, independent hands-on corroboration of a fully scripted agent-driven setup.

support.subject: As an ai-native user, I can have an agent stand up a new backend — schema, auth, and policies — headlessly from the CLI in a script

citations.quote: The Supabase CLI enables you to run the entire Supabase stack locally, on your machine or in a CI environment.
